turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I... I shall endeavor to do so, ma’am. It's just... the house is rather large, and I wouldn't wish to wander about, lest I... lest I should disturb something, or... or get lost, you see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disturb something? Yes… everything is disturbed, is it not? But do not fret, child; a little wandering, a little… disorientation, is quite permissible. Call Estella, I say. Call her now.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. I... I shall attempt it presently. It’s just that the shadows seem to deepen with each moment, and I… I wouldn’t wish to cause any further… disturbance, if you understand.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Presently, you say? A most… deliberate pace, my dear boy. But time, you see, holds little sway within these walls; it lingers, it stagnates… like a forgotten perfume. Call Estella, Pip. Call her.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I... I do apologize, ma’am, for my hesitations. It’s just… the corridors are rather… perplexing, and I wouldn’t want to… to misinterpret the… the arrangement of things, and call someone who isn’t… isn't meant to be called. Estella, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Misinterpret the arrangement? A charming observation, Pip. Everything *is* an arrangement, isn't it? But arrangements, like affections, are so easily… misplaced. Call her, child. Call Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I believe I understand, ma’am. It’s simply that… that the very air seems to… to guide one in certain directions, and I wouldn’t wish to… to interrupt its flow, if you see what I mean. I shall endeavor to locate Miss Estella, ma’am, with as little… as little… disruption as possible.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disruption? My dear Pip, disruption is the very breath of this house. It is all that *remains* of… of a certain expectation. Go, then. Find her. Find Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall, ma’am. Though I confess, the… the shadows do seem to lengthen considerably as one ventures further within. I do hope I shall not… I do hope I shall find Miss Estella without… without causing undue… disturbance, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disturbance? My dear boy, what is disturbance compared to the stillness... the unending stillness that I have known? Go, find her. And when you do, tell her… tell her I expect her to be… pleasing.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. I… I shall endeavor to be as… as unobtrusive as possible in my search, ma’am. It’s just that… that the corridors appear to… to twist and turn in most unexpected ways, and I wouldn’t wish to… to lose my way entirely, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Lose your way? Oh, my dear Pip, losing one's way is often the *only* way to find... anything. It is the wandering, you see, the meandering... it is in the unexpected turns that one encounters the… the forgotten. Go on, then. Do not linger.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall proceed with the utmost care, ma’am. It is… it is quite overwhelming, this house, you see. One feels… one feels rather insignificant amidst such… such grandeur and… and stillness, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Insignificant? Yes, perhaps. All things are insignificant in the face of… of what has been lost, what remains undone. Do you see the dust, Pip? It settles everywhere, you know… a perpetual reminder of what was, and what… will never be.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma’am. I… I do observe the dust, ma’am. It… it clings to everything, doesn’t it? It’s a… a most pervasive quality, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pervasive, you say? Yes, quite. It clings, doesn't it, like… like a memory. A memory that refuses to… to loosen its grip. Come nearer; let me look at you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. It… it does cling, most stubbornly, I should think. I… I wouldn’t wish for such a… a tenacious quality, ma’am, on anyone, you see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Tenacious, you say? A tenacious quality… yes, like a vine, it creeps and clings, doesn’t it? It chokes the light, Pip, it suffocates… and then it withers, leaving only… only the emptiness. Come closer still.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, ma’am. A vine, you say? It… it does seem a rather apt comparison, ma’am. I… I imagine it would be quite distressing to be choked, ma’am, to… to lose the light.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Distressing, yes… distressing indeed. To lose the light… one loses *everything*, doesn't one? Come, Pip, closer still… I wish to see you more clearly.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
